sections.h2: Which Sarasota County office does what with your tax bill?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the job. The property appraiser at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota decides what your parcel is worth and who gets an exemption, and the tax collector mails the bill and takes the money. The rate itself is voted by each taxing body, and neither office controls it.

On the collector's site the real estate notice is described as a single document that merges ad valorem taxes with non-ad valorem assessments, with fire protection and solid waste given as examples. Personal property tied to a business gets its own ad valorem only bill. If the mail brings nothing by mid-November, the collector asks to hear from you and also offers a printable copy online.

Links on the collector's page point to four municipal sites: Sarasota, North Port, Venice and Longboat Key. Counter locations are listed for downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County. Related pages here: Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

sections.h2: What are the Sarasota County tax dates for payment and delinquency?
sections.html:
Bills open for payment on November 1 and the gross amount is due by March 31. Whatever is still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The collector gives a plain example: 2025 tax not paid by then went delinquent on April 1, 2026.

Discounts step down by month: 4 percent for November, 3 for December, 2 for January, 1 for February. Lenders that collect escrow must pay within the 4 percent month, per the collector. For 2026, the appraiser certified the roll on September 29 and the collector reports bills mailed or emailed by October 30.

Hardship tools exist at state level. An owner can ask the collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year, and a homestead owner may file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

sections.h2: How can a Sarasota County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Talk to the appraiser first if you like, but you are free to file with the Value Adjustment Board or sue in circuit court without doing so. The appraiser's page lists all three paths and says they need not be taken in order.

A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM mailing, a date printed on your notice. After a denied exemption or denied assessment transfer, you get 30 days from the letter's mailing date. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board answers filing questions at (941) 861-5279.

Disagree with the board's ruling? A circuit court claim may be filed within 60 days of roll certification. Remember the board looks at value, classification and exemption only. If the tax rate bothers you, speak up at the budget hearing printed on the notice.

sections.h2: What should you bring when you dispute a Sarasota County value?
sections.html:
Documents win these discussions. The appraiser says most issues end in informal talks, and offers sales comparisons and damage records as examples of helpful proof.

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Closing figures for similar houses sold close by.
  • Contractor estimates or photographs for storm or structural damage.
  • Residency papers if a homestead was denied.

The appraiser's phone is 941.861.8200. Hurricane damage has its own page on the appraiser's site.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can shrink a Sarasota County bill?
sections.html:
Homestead leads the list. You need to live in the house as your permanent home on January 1 and apply by March 1, although the office reviews late filings.

State figures describe homestead as up to $50,000, with $25,000 reaching school taxes. Afterward, Save Our Homes caps yearly growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. The appraiser's guide adds:

  • $5,000 for a widow or widower who has not remarried.
  • $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • $5,000 for blindness.
  • $5,000 for a veteran rated at least 10 percent disabled.
  • A homestead discount matching the VA percentage for veterans 65 and over with a permanent combat-related disability.

The collector says voter-approved Amendment 3 reaches the 2027 bill and leaves the 2026 bill as issued.

sections.h2: What follows when Sarasota County tax stays unpaid?
sections.html:
A tax certificate is sold, and eventually a certificate holder can ask for a deed. The collector's own wording is blunt: nonpayment can mean losing the property.

Certificates go on sale by June 1. Bidding is on interest, lowest wins, in quarter-point steps (s. 197.432). A deed application can come two years after April 1 of the issue year, with a $75 fee (s. 197.502). Winning bidders at the clerk's sale put down the larger of 5 percent or $200 (s. 197.542). Our tax deed page goes deeper.

An owner who is behind can pay through closing; the title agent asks the collector for the balance.

sections.h2: How is Sarasota County tax handled at a sale?
sections.html:
The buyer answers to the collector for the whole bill. Between buyer and seller, the closing statement credits the buyer for the months the seller held title, and nothing is wired to the collector as a seller part-payment.

Mailing matters afterward. Tell the appraiser where to send your notices once you move, and forward any real estate bill for a house you sold. Business equipment is different: if you held it on January 1, that year's bill remains yours. Recording details sit in our Sarasota County records guide.

faqs.q: When is Sarasota County property tax due?
faqs.a: Payment opens November 1, and the tax is delinquent after March 31. Early-pay discounts are 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

faqs.q: Where can I pay what I owe in Sarasota County?
faqs.a: Use the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through its website payment options or at offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Sarasota County value?
faqs.a: Yes, with a Value Adjustment Board petition filed within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax bill when a house sells?
faqs.a: The buyer answers to the collector. The seller's months are credited to the buyer on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What if I cannot pay in full?
faqs.a: Ask the collector about an installment plan, which needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year, or a homestead deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31.
